# Prologue: The Gathering Shadow

> *"An empire built upon blood and stolen fire will always hunger for more. When the foundation begins to crack, it does not weep for the fallen; it drags the entire world into the abyss."*
> — *Book of Aurtus, The Third Chronicle*

The Second Age of Man had arrived in fire.

Centuries after the First Age choked beneath nuclear ash and tectonic ruin, the subterranean stasis vaults of the ARC Project had finally cracked. But humanity did not emerge into a healed world of machines and light. They awoke into a fractured, wild frontier where the earth itself had changed. Primal alien crystals had erupted through the scarred crust, bleeding an exotic, living energy known as the Source into every living thing.

Some men became Gifted, mastering kinetic force and crystal flame. The Church of Aurtus arose to shepherd the survivors under the Four Tenets—Life, Order, Balance, and Memory—while the Order of the Wardens patrolled the wilderness with rune-forged steel, keeping the fragile peace between human enclaves and the proud, ancient Silvan tree kingdoms.

Yet in the east, an older darkness had taken root.

An ARC scientist who had awakened generations before the others cast aside her humanity. Imbuing her body with the resonance of the black crystals, she forged herself into an immortal sovereign: the Empress—the Black Queen. From her towering obsidian citadel, she engineered nightmare armies: altered Chimera beasts that stalked the night, telekinetic Chosen bound to her will, and devastating resin siege cannons that spat liquid blue crystal-fire.

When Captain Marcus Gavin’s stasis pod plummeted to earth in the northern frontier, he brought with him the purest, uncorrupted genetics of the First Age. To the Empress, Marcus was the final missing element: the key to synthesizing an invincible army and mastering the pre-collapse military vaults buried in the mantle.

She unleashed Chancellor Juric Rogan to hunt him down.

The war began with the destruction of the mountain outposts. The Empress’s resin cannons shattered ancient walls, scattering the Wardens and driving Marcus and his spectral companion into the deep forests. Yet as Rogan’s subjugation legions marched across the provinces, the balance of power began to fracture from within.

Along the battered eastern seaboard, Messenger Veric Nero survived the massacre of the shore towns, arriving battered and hollow-eyed with Korlin, his faith turning from humble peace toward an unyielding, burning fanaticism that would birth the Sword of the Faithful. In the north, High Warden Lorin Corliss and Grand Adjudicator Uri joined forces with General Erod Durass and the Silvan canopy warriors, fortifying the squat ramparts of the northern abbey against the coming deluge.

And in the secret groves of the Silvan masters, Marcus Gavin submitted to ancient runic grafting, transforming from a lost relic of the past into something the Second Age had not seen in a thousand years: a Runic Mage of the Source.

The lines have been drawn. Empires crumble not from the strength of their enemies, but from the weight of their own tyranny. 

The siege has begun. The dragon awakens. The empire must fall.
